correctness.rationale: For all \(n\ge2\), \(0<t<1\) and interior indices, the coordinate-slack membership test is an exact equivalence. The all-orthant integration has the appropriate positive/negative-sum simplex densities. Beta-integral evaluation and alternating-binomial cancellation yield every coefficient, including its exact normalization, and Minkowski polynomial uniqueness extends the extraction from small positive r to all r. The volume endpoints and strict deficit are checked analytically. An exact rational coefficient checker returned VERIFY_OK for 748 cases; a separate vertex-hull computation agreed in 36 low-dimensional examples. These tests only corroborate the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: An exact complete all-index Godbersen-deficit profile on a canonical one-vertex deformation of a simplex is a motivated quantitative near-equality invariant. In even dimensions the exact central \(t^{n/2}/(1+t^{n/2})\) law exhibits high-order flattening absent from a qualitative equality theorem; the full family can serve as a benchmark for stability conjectures. The work does not assert an unsupported universal stability result or arbitrary finite-table significance.
